name: Walter Judd
bio: a Representative from Minnesota; born in Rising City, Butler County, Nebr., on September 25, 1898; attended the public schools; graduated from the University of Nebraska, Lincoln, Nebr., 1920; MD., University of Nebraska medical school, Lincoln, Nebr., 1923;  United States Army, 1918-1919, private in 1918 and discharged as a second lieutenant, Field Artillery, in 1919; second lieutenant, Field Artillery, Officers Reserve Corps, 1919-1924; instructor of zoology, University of Omaha, 1920-1924; traveling secretary, Student Volunteer Movement in Colleges and Universities in 1924 and 1925; fellowship in surgery, Mayo Foundation, Rochester, Minn., 1932-1934; medical missionary and hospital superintendent in China, under auspices of American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions, 1925-1931 and 1934-1938; engaged in private medical practice in Minneapolis, Minn., 1941-1942; elected as a Republican to the Seventy-eighth and to the nine succeeding Congresses (January 3, 1943-January 3, 1963); unsuccessful candidate for election to the Eighty-eighth Congress in 1962; contributing editor, Reader's Digest, 1963-1976; daily radio commentator and lecturer on international relations and government, 1964-1969; awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by President Ronald Reagan, 1981; resident of Mitchellville, Md.; died on February 13, 1994, in Mitchellville, Md.; interment in Blue Valley Cemetery, Surprise, Nebr.
